g: Any member of an Eastern Romance speaking group, including Romanians, Aromanians, Megleno-Romanians, and Istro-Romanians.
Any member of a Polish ethnographic group (subgroup of Silesians) living around the towns of Cieszyn and Skoczów
Of or relating to the Vlachs.
(now historical) The head of church and state in Montenegro until 1852; the prince bishop.
(mineralogy) A monoclinic-prismatic mineral containing arsenic, calcium, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Of or relating to Maurice de Vlaminck (1876–1958), French painter.
(mineralogy) A monoclinic-prismatic colorless mineral containing oxygen, silicon, sodium, and zirconium.
(Southern Africa) A shallow wetland or minor lake, generally a seasonal one, or the lowland where such a wetland appears seasonally.
Any of various groove-toothed rats of the genus Otomys, found in sub-Saharan Africa.
(mineralogy) A tetragonal-dipyramidal mineral with the chemical formula AlCa₂(SO₄)₂F₂Cl · 4H₂O.
(Internet) A weblog using video as its primary presentation format.
(Internet, intransitive) To contribute to a video weblog.
(Internet, transitive) To post (something) to a video weblog.
A video that can be experienced either as a vlog or as a podcast.
(Philippines, social media, by extension) A content creator, regardless of whether or not they make vlogs.
(Internet) The keeping of a vlog (video weblog).
(Internet) The realm or culture of vlogs; all vlogs taken as a whole.

(derogatory, neologism, very rare) An apology video; a video, typically uploaded to video-sharing service YouTube, in which an Internet celebrity/influencer apologises for, or addresses, public backlash, especially in an insincere manner.
A documentary that is created in the same manner as a vlog or by combining several vlogs together, that is, without a separate film crew.
(UK, dialectal) Nonsense; incoherent or nonsensical talk.
(bacteriology, biochemistry) A lipoprotein from Borrelia mayonii involved in Lyme disease.
(bacteriology, genetics) A gene coding for a lipoprotein (VlsE) in Borrelia mayonii.
(US, chiefly New York, now chiefly in place names) A small swampy or marshy area, especially near a stream.
